clue.text: Monitor to be included at frequent intervals

indicators.note: the word to is told to be included, so it is placed within another word

parts.note: something happening at frequent intervals is regular
taken as written

explanation.surface: A supervisor is told to drop in on things every so often.
explanation.definitionFit: A monitor is a device or person that keeps a process in check, as a controller does.

explanation.surface: A slightly earlier time, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to a certain extent (rather cold) and also preferably, as in would rather go.

clue.text: German count, one having attack first, the writing's on the wall

indicators.note: having the attack first means its letters come ahead of the letter for one

parts.note: Graf is the German title for a count
a fit is a sudden attack, of coughing or rage
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A German nobleman who attacks first sees doom foretold on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writing's on the wall' usually means doom is coming; here it is read literally, as words scrawled on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrawled words or pictures sprayed on public walls are exactly that kind of street writing.

indicators.note: the turn is placed in the middle of the other pieces, signalled by in

parts.note: LA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Louisiana
taken as written
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Someone takes a spin on a lake in Louisiana.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow body of water cut off from the sea by a reef or sandbar is a kind of lake.

clue.text: Thanks Edward who had a trying experience

parts.note: ta is British slang for thank you, and tas is the plural, thanks
Ted is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Edward is thanked for having gone through an ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying' suggests a hard time, but here it means trying something out, as with food.
explanation.definitionFit: To have sampled food or drink is to have had a try of its flavour.

parts.note: to rifle is to search through and steal from
a man is a fellow or chap

explanation.surface: A man robs another soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: An infantryman armed with a long gun is this kind of soldier.

parts.note: a cub is a beginner or apprentice, as in cub reporter

indicators.note: pronouncedly means the word icy is taken as a sound, which is matched by two spoken letters

parts.note: the word icy said out loud sounds like the letters I and C

explanation.surface: A trainee is noticeably frosty and unyielding.
explanation.definitionFit: A solid shape has three dimensions, and a three-dimensional measure is described this way.

clue.text: Squeeze folded cloth applied to the skin

definitions.text: folded cloth applied to the skin

explanation.surface: Pressing a folded cloth against the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means press together; as a noun it is a pad of cloth pressed on a wound or swelling.

clue.text: Exclamation of surprise coming from Roman god

parts.note: by can mean from or by the hand of, as in a poem by Keats
Jove is another name for Jupiter, chief of the Roman gods

explanation.surface: A startled cry from a deity of ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned oath uttered when astonished, invoking a god's name.

clue.text: Short trousers or stole cut badly

indicators.note: something cut badly is mangled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choice between shorts and a poorly tailored wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: These are women's knee-length trousers cut full to look like a skirt.

clue.text: Grates a mixture that makes one's eyes water

indicators.note: a mixture of letters means they are shuffled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grates a blend of ingredients, like onions, that brings tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Police use this irritant vapour to disperse crowds, and it makes people weep.

indicators.note: said means the phrase is spoken and the sound gives the letters entered

parts.note: telly is British slang for television, and a picture is a photo

explanation.surface: A camera lens that makes a picture fit for the television.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-focus camera lens that magnifies distant subjects.

parts.note: reads as a question about a king's daily routine, but asks what a sovereign does while on the throne

explanation.surface: A question about how a king filled his days.
explanation.definitionFit: A king rules, or sits on the throne, for the whole period of his rule.

indicators.note: a new design for the letters means they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A buoyancy jacket stays as wet as ever in a new style.
explanation.walkthrough: The inflatable life vest was nicknamed by RAF airmen after a famously curvaceous film star.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable wartime life vest took its nickname from a buxom Hollywood actress.

clue.text: Keep one point of view and reject disarmament

explanation.surface: Staying firm in an opinion while refusing to lay down arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means refuse to change one's mind; read literally it means to hold on to one's weapons.

parts.note: what a shame means what a pity

indicators.note: developed means the letters change into something new, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: It is a disgrace that the flu has spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disgraceful or outrageous causes a scandal.

clue.text: A cracker reportedly next to a volcano

indicators.note: reportedly means the word cracker is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: the word cracker spoken aloud matches the first part
to can mean next to or against, as in face to face

explanation.surface: A firework is said to be set off beside a volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: The Indonesian volcano erupted catastrophically in 1883.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indonesian island mountain is famous for its 1883 eruption.

parts.note: reads as handing something on during a journey, but means moving past another vehicle on the road

explanation.surface: Something handed on during a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver who pulls out and goes past a slower car on the road has done this.

parts.note: suggests a plane getting ready to fly, but means getting ready to take off a coat or shirt

explanation.surface: An aircraft gets ready to leave the runway.
explanation.definitionFit: Undoing the fastenings on a jacket is the first step in removing it.

indicators.note: consuming means one word swallows the other, so the vegetable goes inside

parts.note: an ape is loosely a monkey
peas are a green vegetable

explanation.surface: Calm an ape by letting it eat its greens.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify someone is to soothe them by giving in to demands.

parts.note: pat means exactly right or perfectly learned, as in off pat
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something perfectly suitable in a movie.

explanation.definitionFit: A green or brown sheen that forms on bronze or old wood is a thin coating.

clue.text: Pyromaniac's continuous attack with object of terror

parts.note: to come under fire is to face continuous shooting
bug is an old word for a bogey or bugbear, a thing feared

explanation.surface: An arsonist keeps up a terrifying assault.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsonist with a compulsion to set things ablaze is given this nickname.

explanation.surface: Hunting down a semi-domesticated creature.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means rummage to discover; as a noun it is a domesticated polecat used for hunting rabbits.

clue.text: Dish up the corned beef again!

definitions.text: Dish up the corned beef again!

parts.words: Dish up the corned beef again!
parts.note: reads as serving a corned beef meal a second time, but means presenting old material in new form

explanation.surface: Serving leftover corned beef once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Corned beef hash is a dish; to serve old ideas up anew is to recycle them.

clue.text: Idler struggling with gravity first, it has no power to fly

definitions.text: it has no power to fly

indicators.note: with gravity first means its letter is placed at the front

parts.note: g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

indicators.note: struggling suggests twisting about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lazy person battles gravity; it cannot fly unaided.
explanation.definitionFit: An engineless aircraft rides air currents and so flies without power.

explanation.surface: Someone who admires their dentist.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist pulls teeth, so is one who removes; a ventilating fan drawing out stale air also bears this name.

clue.text: Responded to something done in a rush

definitions.text: Responded to something done in a rush

parts.words: Responded to something done in a rush
parts.note: describes a hasty reply to an event, a word that also suggests performing once more

explanation.surface: Someone answered a hurried act.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond to a stimulus or event is to answer it with action.

indicators.note: back means the word for pin is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a nail is a pin used in carpentry

explanation.surface: Fix a climbing plant in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A woody vine that hangs in tropical forests is a climber.

clue.text: Field marshal finding room about to come back

parts.note: a kitchen is a room for cooking

indicators.note: to come back means the word for about is turned round

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: A field marshal finds a room to return to.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Kitchener was a British field marshal, famous from First World War recruiting posters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Kitchener was the British field marshal whose face featured on recruitment posters.
